label: PC 19700179
description: Fragment from right side of lifesized statue head: back portion has flat surface which curves gradually outward toward top of fragment, and curves slightly out at point of break on left side (originally center of back of head); back portion forms right angle with side of face, then forms definite depression behind fully preserved ear, ear consists of one raised ridge forming indented semicircle, with extra round area filling in this indentation; remainder of side of face in front of ear is plain, smooth surface. Break on upper edge of fragment indicates an outward curving above the ear and back of head, possibly a helmet, since there is no indication of hair, or any detail of surface of the fragment. Broken edge on bottom, below ear is relatively straight, horizontal.

label: PC 19670013
description: Fragment preserves upper right portion of slightly larger than life-size statue: head was apparently rounded, very wide through cheeks and at eye level; remaining part of the cheek is very smooth and has small, slightly concave area near bottom, forming a flat surface in contrast to cheek itself. Forehead is also slightly concave, due to line of brows at bottom, and very slight thickening of clay at top of fragment, as if for hair, helmet, or the like. Brows, eyes, and nose are smooth, raised masses, relatively sharp in outline, and geometric in overall composition; eye socket is shallowly recessed at right outer corner, deeper beside nose, and almost undifferentiated at bottom where it blends into cheek. General outline is almond shaped, as is that of the bulging eye, which is raised so as to be almost pointed across its center, eye is not set parallel to the socket but is slightly tilted upward on right outer corner. Left eye is preserved only in extreme right corner as small section of socket beside nose, and a small raised area, the inner corner of the eye ball. The nose is sharp and triangular, projecting sharply from the brow ridge, beginning with a point level with the center of the eye socket, roughly triangular on the sides nose has slightly wider, but flat extension at bottom for right nostril left is perhaps abraded, otherwise it is flatter than right and very asymmetrical. Nostrils are two shallow, oblong depressions set off-center in flat underside of nose. Interior surface very rough thickest opposite nose.

label: Item 1320
description: The oval-shaped scarab is pierced lengthwise. The back is represented in a very schematic way. The clypeus and the triangular-shaped head are depicted and are separated from the prothorax by a transverse line. The oval base is surrounded by an engraved linear frame, inside which is a human figure with a falcon's head. The head and legs are depicted in profile and the torso frontally. The figure wears a triangular-shaped kilt, tied at the waist and is represented standing on a neb sign. In front of him is a crocodile. In what has been interpreted as a greeting gesture, the man has his left arm raised next to the animal's head and his right arm stretched along the body. This iconography is dated to the Egyptian XII Dynasty.

label: PC 19680340
description: Preserves part of right end of sima, including cavetto, head scar and rosette. The head scar is narrow at the top and curves broadly out, forming an outline similar to that of head 19680195; however, another type of head may have been used. There are extensive fingermarks around the scar, (which overlap the cavetto; the scar itself does not), and around the rosette. On the right edge of the sima next to the head scar are lumps showing how the clay was smoothed over the back of the head. Much paint is preserved. There is red paint over the entire front surface and the outside of the rosette. The entire inside (except perhaps the central knob) of the rosette is red also, with white overpaint on alternate petals. White paint also appears in the groove bewteen the first and second strigils on the right, and below the third strigil just above the fingermarks around the head scar. Smaller more doubtful traces appear between the fifth and sixth strigils from the right and below the groove between the eighth and ninth.

description: Locus 3 is the circular cut made into limestone bedrock. The cut is situated in the northeastern corner of the trench and has a diameter of about 0.51m. As it was a rock feature, it contained no finds or materials, and as there were minimal finds and no chronologically secure materials recovered in Locus 2, the cut cannot be dated. For example, a ceramic sherd that was removed from a finds bag to be drawn and/or photographed was given an item number. Similarly, a particular bone or lithic that was removed from a finds bag for further analysis was given an item number and was subsequently identified by that item number. Most small finds were assigned item number "1," since they were usually the only item in their finds bag.

label: PC 19970186
description: The rim, body and tondo of a cup is preserved. The body of the cup gently curves upwards from the tondo. The rim projects upwards from the body of the cup, creating a definitive angle. The rim slants slightly inwards towards the interior of the cup. On the exterior the tondo projects downwards from the body of the cup with a low ridge defining the upper portion of the base. Only the very beginning of the curvature into the stem is preserved. On the interior of the cup, the tondo is encirlced by two incised, concentric circles. The larger of the two circles is approximately 0.048 m in diameter while the smaller circle is approximately 0.035 m in diameter. The larger of these two circles corresponds to the exterior attachment point of the base
